children.name: Paracephaelis cinerea

Flowers: (November –) December – March; Fruits: February – September.

Anthetic flowers were also collected in November (4 specs), March (5 specs), May (3 specs); June (1 spec.), and July (2 specs).

children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mid-level epiphyte in closed forest, 2 000 – 2 400 m; often in large numbers in a single tree. Invariably inhabited by a large form of the aggregate ant species Anonychomyrma scrutator.

children.name: Hydnophytum albertisii Becc.

children.name: Hydnophytum alboviride Merr. & L.M.Perry

children.name: Hydnophytum archboldianum Merr. & L.M.Perry

children.name: Hydnophytum buxifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — High-level epiphyte in mossy forest, 2 150 – 2 600 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum caminiferum Wistuba, U.Zimm., Gronem. & Marwinski

children.name: Hydnophytum confertifolium Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — High-level epiphyte of mossy forest, 2 150 – 2 600 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum cordifolium Valeton
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, sea level to 300 m.

children.name: Hydnophytum dauloense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Low to high-level epiphyte in montane forest, 2 400 – 2 800 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants, but collecting rainwater and occupied by a range of invertebrates including cockroaches, centipedes, spiders and on Mt Elimbari the arboreal frog Cophixalus riparius.

children.name: Hydnophytum davisii Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Stunted ridge top Nothofagus forest, at 1 740 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum decipiens Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Mossy forest, 1 420 – 2 150 m; on branches of large trees. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum dentrecastense Jebb & C.R.Huxley
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — This species is found terrestrially on the upper slopes of Mts Pabinama and Bwebwesu of Normanby Island, at c. 600 – 800 m altitude. This is an area of ultrabasic soils with sparse, stunted forest cover. The tuber is not inhabited by ants and nor does it collect rainwater.

children.name: Hydnophytum ellipticum Merr. & L.M.Perry
children.description: Ecology & Habitat — Forest, (? 80 –) 1070 – 1840 m. Tuber not inhabited by ants.

children.name: Hydnophytum fusiforme Jebb & C.R.Huxley

Abundant around Mt Michael. Tuber inhabited by a range of ant species.

Stem ascending or drooping, somewhat straight, simple or branched, terete, glabrous, green, with internodes of 6 - 30 mm long, 2 - 3 mm in diameter. Stipules persistent, glabrous, green, slightly equal to unequal, broadly to narrowly ovate, (4 -) 8 - 10 (- 16) x (3 -) 4 - 8 (- 10) mm, distally often divided up to 2 / 3 th of their length into 2 narrowly ovate to broadly lanceolate, 3 - 5 (- 9) mm long obtuse

children.name: Damnacanthus indicus
children.description:
관목. 높이 4m. 겨울눈 및 소지 정아에 가시가 발달하며, 길이 3-5mm, 달걀형, 끝은 뾰족하고, 아린은 6개이다. 줄기는 마주나기, 혹은 반마주나기이다. 잎자국은 반원형 또는 삼각형이다. 잎 마주나기에서 반마주나기 혹은 짧은 소지에 속생, 잎은 얇고, 좁고 긴달걀형 모양, 크기는 9-15 × 2.5-5.0cm이다. 측맥은 5-6개, 잎 끝은 뾰족하고, 잎 아래는 뾰족하거나 둥글다. 잎 뒷면에 털이 발달하거나 없으며, 약간의 거치가 발달한다. 잎자루는 길이 1-2cm이다. 꽃 암수딴그루, 꽃잎과 꽃받침은 4수이며 수꽃은 10-30개, 암꽃은 2-6개의 꽃이 모여 속생한다. 암꽃에는 수술의 흔적이 있고, 암술대는 2개로 반정도 갈라진다. 꽃받침잎은 삼각형, 꽃잎은 매우 작은 황록색으로 꽃받침열편의 절반 크기이다. 꽃자루는 5-7mm, 털이 있거나 혹은 없다. 열매 및 종자 핵과는 검은색, 열매자루는 5-12mm, 털이 없으며, 종자는 홈이 있다.

개화기 4월말

Shrub or small tree up to 4 m tall, sparsely branched; terminal branchlets terete or slightly laterally compressed, 2.5 - 3.0 mm in diam., glabrous, soon covered with a greyish-beige thin bark. Stipules free, interpetiolar, 2 - 5 mm long, bifid at apex, each lobe deltoid to lanceolate, 1 - 2 mm wide at base, acute to acuminate, glabrous. Leaves with petioles 1.5 - 3.0 cm long, glabrous; blades elliptic, oblong-elliptic oblong-lanceolate, 19 - 34 x 5.5 - 15 cm, acute at base, acumina

children.name: Carapichea cardenasiana C.M.Taylor
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to N. Brazil. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea fimbriflora  C.M.Taylor
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea franquevilleana  C.M.Taylor
children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Colombia to SW. Venezuela. It is a shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea lucida J.G.Jardim & Zappi
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (E. Bahia). It is a shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea necopinata  C.M.Taylor
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea verrucosa C.M.Taylor
children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Colombia to N. Peru and Brazil (Acre). It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea affinis
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Costa Rica to Bolivia. It is a subshrub or shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea ligularis
children.description: The native range of this species is Guianas to N. Brazil. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea guianensis
children.description: Description. Shrub 0.4 - 1.5 m tall, sparsely branched; terminal branchlets terete, 1 - 2 mm in diam., glabrous, soon covered with a buff to pale grey corky bark. Stipules 5 - 9 x 1.5 - 3.0 mm, free, triangular to lanceolate, entire or shortly bifid for up to 3 mm, glabrous outside, villose at the base inside, becoming corky and soon damaged. Leaves with petioles 0.8 - 3.0 cm long, glabrous; blade elliptic, 10 - 18 x 3.3 - 7.5 cm, attenuate and decurrent on the petiole at base, narrowly acuminat

children.name: Carapichea dolichophylla
children.description: Amazonia, Orinoquia, Valle del Magdalena

children.name: Carapichea panurensis
children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Colombia to Brazil (Amazonas). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea klugii
children.description: Amazonia, Guayana y Serranía de La Macarena

children.name: Carapichea maturacensis
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Amazonas) to Brazil (Serra da Neblina). It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea vasivensis
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia (Guainía) to Venezuela (Amazonas). It is a shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea araguariensis
children.description: Description. Shrub, 0.5 - 1.0 m tall, or treelet 2 - 5 m tall, glabrous; terminal branchlets terete, 2 - 4 mm in diam., soon covered with a greyish bark. Stipules shortly sheathing, truncate to very broadly ovate, 1 - 4 x 4.0 - 5.5 mm, entire and obtuse at apex, glabrous, soon corky and fragmenting. Leaves with petioles 0.7 - 2.5 cm long, glabrous; blades elliptic, to oblong-oblanceolate, 11 - 25 x 3.5 - 7.5 cm, acute-decurrent at base, acute and acuminate at apex, acumen narrowly triangular, 0.

children.name: Carapichea crebrinervia
children.description: The native range of this species is N. Brazil. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea pacimonica
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Venezuela to N. Brazil. It is a shrub or tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea sandwithiana
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Bolívar) to Guyana. It is a subshrub or shrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Carapichea urniformis
children.description: Description. Shrub or small tree, up to 4 m tall, much branched; terminal branchlets terete or slightly quadrangular, 3 - 7 mm in diam., somewhat succulent, glabrous, soon covered with a buff corky bark. Stipules free, oblong-ovate, 7 - 12 x 7 - 9 mm, obtuse and entire when young (apical and distal nodes), later splitting into two lobes at older nodes, each lobe oblong-ovate, 4 - 9 mm long, shortly apiculate, soon corky, persistent or fragmenting. Leaves with petioles 1.0 - 3.5 cm long, glabrous

children.name: Carapichea tillettii
children.description: Description. Shrub or treelet 1 - 3 m tall; terminal branchlets terete to slightly quadrangular, 4.0 - 5.5 mm in diam., glabrous, soon covered with a buff corky bark. Stipules shallowly sheathing at base, 3.5 - 8.0 x 5 mm, broadly ovate, glabrous, bilobed or irregularly fimbriate at apex, with lobes 1 - 5 mm long, soon corky and marcescent. Leaves opposite or ternate; petioles 1.5 - 3.0 cm long, glabrous; blades narrowly elliptic or oblong-elliptic, 14 - 25 x 5 - 10 cm, acute to decurrent at bas

children.name: Eumachia
children.description: Eumachia — a genus of magnoliopsidas.

children.name: Eumachia aneityensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Vanuatu (GUILLAUMIN, 1932).

children.name: Eumachia archboldiana  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found on Viti Levu and Kandavu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988). The type of this name was originally said to be deposited at “ USNA ” (FOSBERG, 1942; today NA), but was later cited by SMITH & DARWIN (1988) as being at US. Two specimens in the US collection correspond to the original diagnosis and were previously deposited at NA. These sheets are identified as two parts of one collection, and the first sheet is annotated as the type of this name in Fosberg’s writing. Of th

children.name: Eumachia chlorocalyx  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986).

children.name: Eumachia coffeosperma  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Cameroon and Democratic Republic of Congo, and its subspecies have separate ranges (VERDCOURT, 1977). The holotype of Psychotria coffeosperma was certainly at the B herbarium and has been destroyed. Several duplicates of the type collection are deposited in other herbaria, and the best sheet, with ample material and both flowers and fruits, is here designated as the lectotype.

children.name: Eumachia domatiicola  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Ghana, Nigeria, Cameroon, continental Equatorial Guinea, and Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). RAZAFIMANDIMBISON et al. (2014) cited the type material of Psychotria domatiicola as two specimens deposited at BR, one the holotype and the other an isotype. However these two specimens were not individually designated or identified as to their type status, there or apparently by any previous author. Possibly these sheets were both considered to comprise

children.name: Eumachia evansensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia gossweileri  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the main region of Angola (i. e., not Cabinda; VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia guianensis  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Guianas (TAYLOR, 2005) and northern to central Brazil (DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015).

children.name: Eumachia incompta  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia inconspicua  C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Amazonian Venezuela, Brazil, Peru, and Bolivia. Its known range has been extended since its description, and it is not uncommonly collected in Brazil (C. M. Taylor, pers. obs., INPA).

children.name: Eumachia longistylis  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Gabon (VERDCOURT, 1977). A specimen of this species at P is labelled Mann 887, and appears to be an isotype with a typographical error in the collection number (O. Lachenaud, unpubl. data).

children.name: Eumachia lophoclada  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast, and Ghana (VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia monopedicellata  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Bismarck Archipelago (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia montana  I.M.Turner
children.description: INDONESIA. Sumbawa: 1927, I. Rensch 593.

children.name: Eumachia oleoides  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to New Caledonia (BARRABÉ et al., 2013).

children.name: Eumachia oncocarpa  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species occurs in eastern Polynesia, in Fiji and Samoa (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia purariensis  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Papua New Guinea (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia ramisulca  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). It was illlustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 815, fig. 5).

children.name: Eumachia sciadephora  Razafim. & C.M.Taylor
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Nigeria, and Cameroon (VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia sclerocarpa  Barrabé, C.M.Taylor & Razafim.
children.description: Notes. – This species is endemic to Savaii in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986). The K isotype was studied physically, but it has not been databased or imaged and therefore does not have a barcode or other identifying accession number.

children.name: Eumachia wilhelminensis  Delprete & J.H.Kirkbr.
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Surinam and northeastern Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005). The epithet of this species was misspelled by TAYLOR (2005) as wilhemensis.

children.name: Eumachia carnea
children.description: Notes. – WHISTLER (1986) reported this species from Fiji, Tonga, and Samoa, and circumscribed it to include Psychotria oncocarpa K. Schum. In contrast SMITH & DARWIN (1988) regarded these as two separate species, and considered Eumachia carnea to be restricted to Tonga; SMITH & DARWIN (1988) are followed here.

children.name: Eumachia chaenotricha
children.description: Notes. – This species is commonly collected from eastern Brazil through northern Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy.

children.name: Eumachia cymuligera
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in southeastern Brazil and northern Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005). TAYLOR (2005) reported the place of deposit of the holotype of Mapouria cymuligera at M, but the specimen at BR with an annotation in Müller’s hand appears to be the actual holotype. Another of M. cymuligera isotype was formerly deposited at B but has been destroyed (photo F neg. # 25701). The identity of M. umbelluligera has not been clear until recently. Its type matches that of M. cymuligera, and in fa

children.name: Eumachia depauperata
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in dry vegetation, including caatinga, carrasco, restinga, and semideciduous forest, in Ceará, Paraíba, and Rio de Janeiro in eastern Brazil. Mapouria depauperata was described in an addendum to Müller’s main flora treatment for Brazil, and this name has been overlooked. Also the species Margaritopsis carrascoana has been poorly documented until recently. The type of Mapouria depauperata is not separable from Margaritopsis carrascoana, and these names are synonymiz

children.name: Eumachia inaequifolia
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Bahia and Minas Gerais in eastern Brazil. The identity of Psychotria inaequifolia has been unclear for some time, but it has now been documented by several good collections. These collections show the characteristic flattened ridged internodes, bilobed stipules with glandular lobes and the basal portion becoming hard and yellowed, and red fruits of Eumachia. This species is additionally characterized by its leaves with reticulated higher-order venation that is r

children.name: Eumachia albert-smithii
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia and also is disjunct in Suriname (TAYLOR, 2005). DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) reported that this species is “ widespread in South America ”, but it may be restricted to the western Amazon basin. The Suriname plants are only known in immature fruit, and are included in this species provisionally. These have smaller inflorescences as well as a markedly disjunct distribution, and probably deserve re-evaluation a

children.name: Eumachia astrellantha
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in the Guianas and Amazonian Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and northern Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) reported that this species is found “ throughout Brazil ” but it seems to be restricted to the Amazon basin. Eumachia astrellantha has often been confused with E. chaenotricha, which is found widely in eastern and southeastern Brazil.

children.name: Eumachia boliviana
children.description: PERU. Coronel Portillo, Chara del Sr Cesar Vela, 25 x 1972, J. Sibunke V. 5461.

children.name: Eumachia cephalantha
children.description: BRAZIL. Sao Paulo: Piracicaba, estrada para Limeira, 14 vii 1993, V. C. Souza et al. 6001.

children.name: Eumachia deinocalyx
children.description: Note. – This species was known from the Guianas and eastern through southern Venezuela (TAYLOR, 2005), and has also been recently reported from Amazonian northern Brazil (DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015; e. g., Farney & Batista 2031, Prance et al. 10647, both at both MO and NY).

children.name: Eumachia kappleri
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Guianas, in Amazonian Venezuela, Brazil, and Colombia, and in Costa Rica (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia microdon
children.description: PANAMA. OIS, 16 vi 1924, L. A. M. Riley SERA 149.

children.name: Eumachia nana
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005; DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE, 2015). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. The type locality was reported by Ule as Amazonas in Brazil, but the Rio JuruáMirim is actually in today’s Brazilian state of Acre and at the time Ule was there, Acre was still part of Bolivia. The holotype was deposited at B and has been destroyed (photo F neg. # 467).

children.name: Eumachia pallidinervia
children.description: Note. – This species is found in southern Venezuela (TAYLOR et al., 2004; TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia paupertina
children.description: Note. – This species is found in southern Venezuela (TAYLOR et al., 2004; TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia podocephala
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Amazonian Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil, and Peru (TAYLOR, 2005). See TAYLOR (2005) and DELPRETE & KIRKBRIDE (2015) for synonymy. See TAYLOR (2005) also for discussion of the nomenclatural confusion between this species and the unrelated species Psychotria turbinella var. sororiella (Müll. Arg.) Steyerm. TAYLOR (2005) attempted to designate a duplicate of the type collection in the Martius herbarium at M, which Müller likely studied, as the lectotype for Mapouria

children.name: Eumachia abrupta
children.description: TANZANIA. Uzungwa Mountain NP, stream west of Kilombaro village, 12 xi 1997, P. A. & W. R. Q. Luke 5151.

children.name: Eumachia acuifolia
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in eastern Cuba (LIOGIER, 1963). It has been assumed by various authors that the holotype of Margaritopsis acuifolia is among Wright’s materials at GH, but his specimen numbering is complicated and many of his types need further study.

children.name: Eumachia collina
children.description: NEW CALEDONIA. Exploitation forestiere Guiraud piste en direction de Mt Ades (800 – 850 m), sol ferallitique sur peridotites, 25 iii 1988, Jaffre 2951.

children.name: Eumachia forsteriana
children.description: Notes. – This species occurs in Fiji, Samoa and Tonga (WHISTLER, 1986; SMITH & DARWIN, 1988). WHISTLER recognized two varieties of this species, but SMITH & DARWIN synonymized them; SMITH & DARWIN are followed here.

children.name: Eumachia hassleriana
children.description: Notes. – This species was known from Paraguay (TAYLOR, 2005) and has recently also been confirmed from eastern and northeastern Brazil (e. g., Kuhlmann 3958, MO and SP; Stannard et al. H 51938, MO). Four duplicates of the type collection of Rudgea hassleriana are deposited at G, where Chodat worked. The only specimen in his personal herbarium has original drawings and is here considered the holotype.

children.name: Eumachia horsfieldiana
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Java in Indonesia (GOVAERTS et al., 2015). This species has been compared to or confused with Psychotria rostrata Blume. More study will be needed to clarify the identity of the latter.

children.name: Eumachia huallagae
children.description: Note. – This species is known from Amazonian Peru, Bolivia, and western Brazil (TAYLOR, 2005) and has also recently been documented in Ecuador (G. Villa & P. Alvia 982, MO).

children.name: Eumachia impatiens
children.description: Note. – This species is found from Nicaragua to northwestern Colombia (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia insidens
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Nigeria, Liberia, and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea, and its subspecies have separate ranges (VERDCOURT, 1977). The name Psychotria insidens was based on collections made by Mann in Bioko and deposited at K, which VERDCOURT (1975: 269) detailed as the syntypes Mann 310 and Mann 1155. This name has apparently not been typified further, so a lectotype is designated here. The collection Mann 310 has more label data, a duplicate deposited in another herbarium, and matu

children.name: Eumachia lyciiflora
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to New Caledonia (BARRABÉ et al., 2013).

children.name: Eumachia membranacea
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia membranifolia
children.description: Notes. – This species occurs in Papua New Guinea and the Philippines (SOHMER, 1988; SOHMER & DAVIS, 2007). An illustration was presented by SOHMER & DAVIS (2007: 117, fig. 61).

children.name: Eumachia merrilliana
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to the Solomon Islands (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia nutans
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Cuba and Hispaniola (LIOGIER, 1963, 1995). See TAYLOR (2005) for synonymy.

children.name: Eumachia obanensis
children.description: CAMEROON. Prov. Sud-Oeust: Dept Fako, Bakingili 50 – 300 m trail to Mt Cameroon, 25 vii 1984, S. A. Thompson & J. E. Rawlins 1662.

children.name: Eumachia poggei
children.description: Notes. – This species was described from Democratic Republic of Congo, and VERDCOURT (1977) considered it poorly known. He noted that it is apparently similar to Eumachia oddonii, and may even be the same in which case the name E. poggei has priority over E. oddonii. Both of these names are provisionally accepted here following VERDCOURT. Psychotria poggei was described based on several syntypes that were deposited at B and have since been destroyed. No duplicates of these have so far been locat

children.name: Eumachia rotundifolia
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Cabinda in northern Angola (VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia schmielei
children.description: Note. – This species occurs in the Bismarck Archipelago and the Solomon Islands (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia viridicalyx
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Cameroon, and in Cabinda in northern Angola (VERDCOURT, 1977).

children.name: Eumachia wildemaniana
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Republic of Congo and Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). Four syntype specimens of Psychotria wildemaniana were cited by VERDCOURT (1977: 793), but some have not been located in this present study so the typification of this name cannot be resolved here.

children.name: Eumachia agustinae
children.description: Note. – This species is found in eastern Cuba (LIOGIER, 1963).

children.name: Eumachia amoena
children.description: Note. – This species is found on Viti Levu and Vanua Levu in Fiji (SMITH & DARWIN, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia balabacensis
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in the Philippines, where it is known from several scattered islands (SOHMER & DAVIS, 2007). It was illustrated by SOHMER & DAVIS (2007: 116, fig. 60). They cited the date of the type collection as January 1913, however the date on the label is August 1913.

children.name: Eumachia cupulicalyx
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Liberia (VERDCOURT, 1977). It was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 800, fig. 3).

children.name: Eumachia damasiana
children.description: PAPUA NEW GUINEA. New Britain: north end of Lake Daketana on Willhaumez Peninsula, 30 v 1973, R. S. Isles et al. NGF 32277.

children.name: Eumachia galorei
children.description: Note. – This species occurs from the Bismarck Archipelago to Papua New Guinea (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia geminodens
children.description: Notes. – This species is endemic to Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986). The holotype was deposited at B, where Schumann worked, but has been destroyed.

children.name: Eumachia goodenoughiensis
children.description: Note. – This species is found in Papua New Guinea (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia haematocarpa
children.description: Note. – This species is found from Nicaragua to northwestern Ecuador (TAYLOR, 2005).

children.name: Eumachia lanceifolia
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Haiti (LIOGIER, 1995). The holotype specimen deposited at B, where Urban worked, has been destroyed. Two duplicates of the type collection are deposited in Ekman’s main collection at S, and the sheet with more material on it is here designated as the lectotype.

children.name: Eumachia leptothyrsa
children.description: PAPUA NEW GUINEA. Madang Province: Ramu Subprovince, Walium Station, 20 iv 1979, Sohmer & Katik LAE 75127.

children.name: Eumachia letouzeyi
children.description: Ξ Chazaliella letouzeyi Robbr. in Bull. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat., B, Adansonia. 11: 344. 1990.

children.name: Eumachia macrocarpa
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Gabon and Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). It was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 795, fig. 2). Two specimens of the type of Chazaliella macrocarpa Verdc. are deposited at BR, one with a label and an annotation by VERDCOURT with this name, an another with no label, no annotation with any name, a barcode number that indicates it was accessioned separately and later than the first specimen, and no indication that it was studied by Verdcourt, who rou

children.name: Eumachia novohiberiensis
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Bismarck Archipelago (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia obovoidea
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Cameroon and eastern to central Democratic Republic of Congo (VERDCOURT, 1977). Its typical subspecies was illustrated by VERDCOURT (1977: 805, fig. 4). Plants of Eumachia obovoidea are often notable for their corky or thickened stems. Two duplicates of the type specimen of Chazaliella obovoidea are deposited at BR, where the holotype was designated in the protologue without further detail. One of these specimens has a collection label, an annotation with this n

children.name: Eumachia oddonii
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Nigeria, Cameroon, Republic of Congo, and Democratic Republic of Congo. The type material of this name was cited by VERDCOURT (1977: 799) as two collections deposited at BR. One collection, Oddon in Gillet 3746, has not been seen so this name cannot be further typified here. Verdcourt considered Eumachia poggei to be of somewhat unclear identity, but similar to or perhaps not distinct from E. oddonii.

children.name: Eumachia ovoidea
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in continental southeastern Asia, in Vietnam and Cambodia (GOVAERTS et al., 2015). RUHSAM et al. (2008) concluded that this species does not belong to Chassalia, and transferred it to Psychotria but did not designate a lectotype. This species has the characters of Eumachia rather than Psychotria, and does not match any other Eumachia species treated here. Therefore this name is transferred to Eumachia, but this species is not well understood so but more study will

children.name: Eumachia parviflora
children.description: Note. – This species was known to VERDCOURT (1980) only from the type specimen, from Cabinda in northern Angola.

children.name: Eumachia saidoriensis
children.description: Note. – This species is found in the Bismarck Archipelago (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia samoana
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Savaii and Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986).

children.name: Eumachia savaiiensis
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Savaii and Upolu in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986).

children.name: Eumachia straminea
children.description: Note. – This species is found in continental southeastern Asia, in Vietnam and southeastern and southern China (CHEN & TAYLOR, 2011: 300).

children.name: Eumachia trichostoma
children.description: Note. – This species occurs in the Solomon Islands and perhaps also Vanuatu (SOHMER, 1988).

children.name: Eumachia triflora
children.description: Notes. – This species is found in Haiti (LIOGIER, 1995). The holotype specimen of Margaritopsis triflora at B, where Urban worked, has been destroyed. Two duplicates of the type collection are deposited in Ekman’s main herbarium at S, and one of these has several mature flowers and is here designated the lectotype.

children.name: Eumachia vaupelii
children.description: Note. – This species is endemic to Savaii in Samoa (WHISTLER, 1986).

children.name: Eumachia extensa
